notes: Each row is a distinct abstract language-contact unit, not a day, lesson, quest, scene or NPC interaction.

introduce_m lists first R according to LANGUAGE_MAP; introduce_g lists first meaningful R of G according to LANGUAGE_PROGRESSION; first_p lists first independent productive intent for 42 M, never for receptive-only M.
revisit_m is a proposed opportunity to reuse an earlier M with a changed context; not evidence of mastery or a performed test.
The short contrasts are semantic-design tests, not language-parser whitelists; examples may use familiar lexical placeholders.
Load must be judged as a vector of independent dimensions; counts of M/G IDs are planning proxies, NOT calibrated difficulty.
A second independent-P opportunity was added at P2b for location and P3c for preferences, to avoid packing multiple first productive intentions into the same unit.
lexical_anchors are selected expression *candidates* from the 29-group independent language catalogue, NOT a hard number of new words in a day; context_optional is never a requirement.

A few elementary expressions are placed earlier than their catalogue group horizon because the independent M/G map uses them earlier (e.g. ich/du, verstehen, heute/morgen); this is deliberate and must not be confused with teaching entire theme early.
Contemporary lesson/domain examples inside one unit are alternative variants, not simultaneous mandatory unknown vocabulary; background R/E grammar does not create forced productive form.
P6 has distributed integration rather than a single nine-target mega-test: a P6 unit contains at most five planned revisits and never new required M/G.
outcome_candidates provide earlier practice and P6 transfer candidates for each 6 R + 7 W LO; they are not an exam, passing score or proof of mastery.
Independent first-R prerequisites for M08/M22/M27/M30/M55 and G24/G25/G32 are explicitly covered by the lexical anchor schedule.
